findings_to_judge.finding: UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide implies Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $156-176mm, but the company itself quantified the prior-year Q4 as depressed by $40-50mm of cyber-incident adjusted EBITDA, so on a cyber-clean basis Q4 FY26 EBITDA is roughly flat to +13% (mid ~+3%) against reported growth of +34% to +52%, and against +23.4% in Q2 and +16.6% in Q3 — the underlying run-rate that has to support a ~$745-760mm FY27 guide on the way to the $800mm FY28 Investor Day target has decelerated to near zero.

SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2 million in May 2025 to 36.6 million in May 2026 (-13%, faster than CBO projected, with Arizona -55%, Florida -22%), and this data was published on 2026-08-21 — after UNFI last guided on 2026-06-09; UNFI's Conventional ($3.136bn) plus Retail ($515mm) segments were ~47% of Q3 FY26 net sales and are precisely the SNAP-exposed channels.

Both listed natural-channel retailers reported negative traffic inside UNFI's Q4 window (2026-05-03 to 2026-08-01): Natural Grocers' quarter ended 2026-06-30 showed daily-average comps +1.2% built entirely on a +3.1% basket with transaction count -1.8% and gross margin down 60bp, and Sprouts' June quarter showed comps -1% with management citing weaker June trends — while UNFI's Natural segment (+4.4% in Q3) is the only growing part of the company and the pillar of the FY27 return-to-growth guide.

Amazon's physical-stores net sales — the reported line for Whole Foods, UNFI's largest customer at roughly a quarter of net sales — were $5,794mm in the June-2026 quarter versus $5,595mm a year earlier, +4% and +4% excluding FX, essentially unchanged from the +4.6% March-quarter pace, covering two-thirds of UNFI's Q4.

UNFI pulled its Q4/full-year report forward roughly three weeks against a stable four-year pattern — 2026-09-08 versus 2025-09-30, 2024-10-01 and late September in the two prior years — and announced the new date on 2026-08-10, the exact day the incoming CFO started, five and a half weeks after a 1 August fiscal year end.

The initial FY27 guide — the single largest swing factor in this print — will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10, four weeks before, as part of four senior changes in seven weeks around the fiscal year end: Matteo Tarditi moved off CFO to President/COO, Alfredo Luchini arrived as CFO from Carrier, supply-chain head Mark Bushway was announced as departing 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased in the role on 2026-08-24.

UNFI's fuel hedge book is a $5m Level-2 current asset as of 2026-05-02 (up from $1m at 2026-01-31) - trivially small against a $1.87/gal year-over-year diesel move - and being entirely current it expires inside FY27, exactly the year whose guide is set on 8 September, with US on-highway diesel at $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 (+$1.865 YoY) after having fallen to $4.578 on 2026-07-06.

Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, which buys 69% of its product from UNFI, reported its quarter ended 2026-06-30 - sitting entirely inside UNFI's Q4 - with net sales up only 1.8%, daily average transaction COUNT down 1.8%, gross margin down 60bp on unfavourable mix and higher freight, and cut the top end of both its FY26 EPS guide ($2.15 to $2.11) and its comp guide (2.5% to 2.0%), all against a prior-year base that its own release says was distorted by the cybersecurity incident at its primary distributor.

Five senior officer changes between 2026-07-09 and 2026-08-24 - CFO Matteo Tarditi moved to President/COO, Louis Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, external hire Alfredo Luchini (ex-Carrier) became CFO on 2026-08-10, Chief Supply Chain Officer Mark Bushway exits 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased to serve on 2026-08-24 - so a CFO four weeks into the seat delivers UNFI's first multi-year guide, and the Echols departure was disclosed only in an exit Form 4 with no 8-K and no press release.
